title: Shadow Bridge: cost-aware shadowing pipeline with tenant isolation and safe sampling
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: build a production-ready shadowing pipeline ("Shadow Bridge") that duplicates production requests to candidate model backends while enforcing per-tenant cost limits, safe sampling, isolation, and automatic rollback triggers. This ticket covers: sampling algorithms, per-tenant credit fencing, request tagging and idempotency, latency & quality-based fallback, and observability + runbooks. Constraints: must add near-zero latency overhead to production path (target < 3ms median), cannot overrun tenant budget, and must preserve request privacy (no additional PII retention). Design decisions so far: use an asynchronous, non-blocking duplicator service downstream of the gateway to avoid head-of-line latency; attach opaque shadow headers and a shadow_id for traceability; run candidate requests in a sandboxed pool with isolated GPU quota; maintain a per-tenant credit ledger in the metering service to gate sampling; sampling rates are dynamic and decayed by observed cost burn and quality signal. We will not mirror streaming token-level traffic in Phase 1 — only request-level duplication for short responses to reduce initial complexity. The design favors cost-safety and clear observability over maximizing raw shadow volume in early rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Asynchronous duplicator that tags shadow requests with shadow_id and tenant_id and returns immediately on production path
Per-tenant credit fence that prevents shadowing if tenant spend >= configured shadow_budget
Adaptive sampler that supports static percentage, credit-budgeted sampling, and priority overrides for flagged tenants
Sandboxed execution pool for candidate backends with GPU quota isolation and throttling
Observable metrics: shadow_tokens_burned, shadow_requests_dropped_by_budget, shadow_latency_p50/p95, shadow_quality_regressions
Dashboards and alerts (cost burn > 5% of monthly budget in 1h window) and automatic rollback trigger integrated with rollout controller
Integration tests simulating tenant exhaustion, slow candidate backend, and idempotent replays
Runbook with step-by-step rollback and tenant notification templates
comments: 2026-02-21 | Asha Kapoor: Initial triage and proposal added. Decided to stage work in three phases: (1) safe async duplication + per-tenant credits, (2) adaptive sampling and quality signal integration, (3) token-level streaming support. Linked design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INFR/Shadow+Bridge+Design

2026-02-26 | Leah Morgan (SRE review): Raised concern about stateful credit ledger availability during region failover. Action: add local LRU cache and lease-based fallback to avoid blocking production. Assigned ENG-418900 for ledger HA follow-up.

2026-03-02 | Sanjay Patel (ML infra): Suggested sandbox pools should run with a lower priority and use eviction-friendly allocator to avoid interference with Dedicated capacity. We agreed on soft-quota + eviction callback. Added note to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-05 | Miguel Santos: Prototype of duplicator service up in staging. CPU overhead measured: +1.8ms median on staging gateway. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/1824

2026-03-08 | Olivia Chen (QA): Integration test coverage added for budget exhaustion and slow candidate. Found a race where two concurrent sampler updates caused momentary double-dipping; mitigation implemented by swapping to CAS update on ledger (PR referenced above).
2026-03-10 | PM review (Daniel Kim): Requested release gating: must pass chaos test for gateway failover and ensure rollback hook is wired to release manager UI. Added to release checklist.

2026-03-10 | Miguel Santos: Deploy plan drafted: staging (5% shadow) -> sandbox tenants (10–20 tenants) -> opt-in pilot (3 customers) -> gradual ramp with cost alarms. Dashboard for pilot: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/shadow-bridge
